reads: ~/.cache/arda_at (Amanyë Tenceli, mirrored) -- FACTS ONLY, no prose republished
encoding: ConScript Unicode Registry tengwar, U+E000 onward
rule: The General Use permits the vowel-sign over EITHER the preceding or the following tengwa -- though not both in one document. 8 attested specimens put it following, 4 preceding. THIS ARCHIVE OFFERS BOTH AND DEFAULTS TO NEITHER.

following.rule: the vowel-sign sits over the tengwa that FOLLOWS it -- the commoner practice, and the one the Writing Lab offered as though it were the only one
following.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use, reading the Mellonath Daeron specimens: it assigns the following-tengwa placement to these eight. [EXT] -- Björkman's reading, and the SPECIMEN NUMBERS are the checkable part, not his sentence.

preceding.rule: the vowel-sign sits over the tengwa that PRECEDES it, as in the classical Quenya mode
preceding.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use: it assigns the preceding-tengwa placement to these four specimens. [EXT] -- Björkman's reading.

rules.says: the mode is named 'the general use' in DTS 58, and is there stated to be 'applicable to both S[indarin] and Q[uenya]'
rules.cite: DTS 58, quoted in Amanyë Tenceli, General Use.

rules.what: either placement, never both in one document
rules.says: the General Use permits the vowel-sign over EITHER the preceding or the following tengwa -- though not both in the same document
rules.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use, citing Appendix E. 12 specimens counted: 8 following, 4 preceding.

rules.says: a bar above a consonant marks that it is preceded by the nasal of the same series -- nt, mp, nk
rules.cite: Appendix E, The Tengwar, quoted in Amanyë Tenceli: 'a bar (or a sign like a Spanish tilde) placed above a consonant was often used to indicate that it was preceded by the nasal of the same series (as in nt, mp, or nk)'.

rules.says: the same bar on a nasal marks it as preceded by itself, in effect doubling it
rules.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use -- Björkman's inference from the nasal bar, and marked as his rather than as Appendix E's.

rules.says: a following w is written with a modified u-curl
rules.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use: 'A following w ... is written with the "modified u-curl" alluded to in AppE.'

rules.says: a following s is shown by a curl extending from the tengwa, commonly from its rightmost bow
vowels in the General Use are represented primarily by vowel-marks, not by full letters
rules.cite: Amanyë Tenceli, General Use, citing DTS 58.

unresolved.the per-letter consonant assignments: NOT ESTABLISHED. Amanyë Tenceli renders its General Use consonant chart as an IMAGE (teng_general_cons1.gif, empty alt text), and Appendix E's tengwar tables are image-held in the edition this archive holds -- 'general use' occurs ZERO times in the whole of The Lord of the Rings, searched through ardatext.fold(). The archive will not publish a letter-value it has not read. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a reading of the Appendix E plate for the general use, or of DTS 58, recorded [I-H] as the Quenya mode's tehtar already are.
unresolved.which placement a given text should use: NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE MODE. It is a property of the document, not of the mode, and the sources give 8 specimens one way and 4 the other. A transcriber must ASK, and this dataset therefore offers it as a parameter rather than a default.
unresolved.the older general use: NAMED AND NOT DESCRIBED. Amanyë Tenceli reports a table 'Feänorian Alphabet. General or Phonetic form' in which the third series is velar and the fourth labiovelar -- a different mode of the same name, cited to R24 and to Arden R. Smith. The archive records that it exists and does not reconstruct it.

note: A MODE OF RULES, not of letters. What the sources settle about the General Use is how it BEHAVES -- the placement choice, the nasal bar, the following-s curl, the labial u-curl. What they do not settle here is which tengwa writes which consonant, because that table is a picture in every source this archive holds. The refusal is named in `unresolved` rather than left as an absence.
